notes:
Summary: mid-market ecommerce SaaS (post-purchase support platform) - wants to replace rule-based replies + paginated order lookups with an agent that calls internal order-service for returns/shipping status. Primary objective is to meet strict p95 latency SLOs while keeping token cost manageable during peak season.

Stakeholders: VP Product (Claire Nguyen) - product lead; Head of Engineering (Diego Morales) - infra/POC owner; Head of Ops (Riya Shah) - cares about SLA & uptime for BFCM peaks.

Key requirements / constraints:
- Workload: multi-turn support agent + microtool calling (order lookup, refund status, return label generation) + short structured responses for CSR handoff.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 450ms for agent responses during normal traffic; target p95 <= 600ms during peak (black friday/cyberweek). Streaming output required for progressive answer display in web widget.
- Throughput & seasonality: baseline 40 qps; expected Black Friday spikes up to ~240 qps (6x) for 6 hours/day for ~7 days. Needs autoscale/burst capacity and predictable tail latency.
- Model prefs: open to Llama2-style variants for cost; wants Redwood-verified performance profiles. Must support function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, traceability from widget -> model call -> tool-call.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required; SSO (Okta) mandatory; want KMS integration for encryption at rest; data residency (US + EU customers) - retention controls.

POC notes so far:
- Running hosted_api POC baseline (single region us-west). Initial synthetic perf run (3k concurrent simulated users, short chat flows) shows p95 ~= 520ms with default batching. SE recommended: enable prefix KV cache, enable continuous batching cut to 16ms, lower max tokens for assistant->tool transitions.
- Tool-calling latency dominated by order-service RPC (avg 45ms) + model serialization; observed additional 80-120ms for longer tool calls when streaming enabled. Need to validate streaming with tool-call fan-out.
- Cost sensitivity: product team worried about long multi-turn histories for returns (customers often do 6-8 turns). Interested in Optimize feature recommendations for batching + quantization when moving to Dedicated.

Quotes & call snippets:
- "If p95 slips over 600ms during BF we lose conversion and ops load spikes — we need guarantees or a deterministic fallback." — Claire Nguyen (VP Product)
- "We like the API ergonomics; show us Dedicated economics for 3 regions + burst." — Diego Morales (Head Eng)

Next actions (short):
- Complete 2-week perf POC (hosted) and collect real widget traces (deadline 2025-04-15).
- Run Dedicated baseline in parallel to compare p95 under identical load (Arjun to provision).
- Security: upload SOC2 + SSO docs; schedule KMS tech call (Lena + Security team).
- Pricing: generate 12-month Dedicated commit + burst add-on proposal ahead of 2025-04-10 workshop.

Open questions / risks:
- Exact SLA wording for burst capacity during BFCM (legal to confirm).
- KMS HSM requirements for EU customers (legal/infra).
- Persistent conversation context retention policy vs token cost tradeoff (ops wants 30-day retention for fraud ops).
